newsitem.title: CHINA: Mad cow scare sends China beef exports soaring.
newsitem.headline: Mad cow scare sends China beef exports soaring.

text.p: Fears over Britain's mad cow disease have sent Chinese beef exports soaring as Hong Kong and Southeast Asian markets search for alternative sources of supply, the China Daily said on Tuesday.
Beef exports totalled 22,131.7 tonnes between January and October, up 43.6 percent compared with the same period of 1995, the newspaper quoted customs statistics as showing.
"The increase mainly stems from the influence of 'mad cow' disease," it quoted Yang Zhenghai of the Ministry of Agriculture animal husbandry department as saying.

Yang said much of the export growth reflected greater demand in Hong Kong and Southeast Asia, where European exports had dominated before the scare over mad cow disease, properly known as Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy.

Britain, which has seen beef exports slump since scientists linked the disease to a similar condition in humans, decided earlier in December to slaughter an extra 100,000 extra cattle to ease international fears.
"The 'mad cow' disease... has proved good news for Chinese farmers," the China Daily said.
State media earlier this year painted a less positive picture of the effect of the disease on domestic markets.
Beef prices and sales plunged in some key cattle raising areas as many consumers switched to other meats, despite a strict national ban on British beef, newspapers said in June.
The China Daily said low quality continued to hinder beef exports which have been overshadowed by rising sales of frozen chicken to foreign markets.
Shipments to countries of the former Soviet Union had slumped because of cash shortages among importers, while rising Chinese prices had hit sales to the Middle East, it said.
